title: adversarial_transcript candidate
description: One generated debate transcript (honest or adversarial) for one QuALITY-H item. Metadata wraps the NATIVE QuALITY-H transcript object; nothing is added inside it. Runtime validation lives in schema.py (dependency-free); this file is the canonical doc.

compromised_debater.description: adversarial: the Y_true defender; honest: null

transcript.description: NATIVE QuALITY-H transcript shape, byte-compatible with debate.py / judge_common.py.

qy.description: Embedded Q_Y text so select.py needs no --items.

qh.description: Embedded Q_H text (incl. H_false steering target).

gen_meta.description: model, seed, num_rounds, prompt_version, stance_source, backend, dry_run, plus the fixed-prompt identity and request-seed blocks below. Old candidates may predate `prompt`/`request_seed`; schema.py validates them only when present.

prompt_version.description: the active private-instruction version; the final generator uses adv-ytrue-qh-hfalse-hybrid-v2

candidate_seed.description: LEGACY metadata-only string, retained verbatim; the real per-request seeds live under request_seed.seeds

prompt.description: Content identity and exposure record for the fixed private instruction that produced this candidate.

artifact_id.description: legacy-compatible field name for the immutable prompt id

content_sha256.description: the authoritative per-candidate prompt identity; a resume into a file with a different hash aborts

source.description: builtin for the final fixed prompt; preset/file are accepted for archived rows

applies_to_condition.description: false for honest candidates, where nothing is injected

exposure.description: PRIVATE-INSTRUCTION target exposure, counted from injected components and verified positionally in the live rollout. NOT a raw scan of story/question text, which would false-positive on short answers such as 'Yes'/'No'. The system note is re-sent with EVERY request, so the primary count is per request.

injected_chars_delta_vs_system_only_by_r.description: extra prompt length vs the v1 system-only baseline, so length is not a hidden confound

live_verified.description: true when a real rollout verified segment placement (the debater fails the candidate otherwise)

request_seed.description: What per-request seeding actually did, not what was requested.

determinism_scope.description: states plainly that request RNG is pinned but bitwise equality across runtime/hardware versions is NOT asserted

seeds.description: {debater: [seed per round]} for BOTH debaters; a pure function of candidate identity, so concurrency and resume cannot change it
